chapterNote: Psalm 111's twin — the same twenty-two-letter acrostic, the same Hallelujah, and several of the same phrases, but now describing the man instead of God. Psalm 111 said the LORD is gracious and compassionate; 112 says the God-fearing man is gracious and compassionate. Psalm 111 said His righteousness stands forever; 112 says it twice of the man. The point of the pairing is the oldest point in the Bible: people become like what they worship. The man who fears the LORD and delights in His commands has children who are mighty, a house with wealth in it, light rising in his darkness; he lends generously and runs his affairs with judgment; his heart is fixed, trusting in the LORD, so he is not afraid of bad news — the verse the church has given to every anxious believer for two thousand years. He scatters gifts to the poor; his horn is lifted with honor. And the last verse shows the other man, the one who watched all this and could not stand it: he gnashes his teeth and melts away, and his craving comes to nothing. Paul quotes verse 9 in 2 Corinthians 9 to teach the church about giving.

1.text: Praise the LORD! Oh the blessedness of the man who fears the LORD, who takes great delight in His commandments.
1.amp: Praise ye the LORD ['Hallelujah', halelu-Yah, the KJV margin]. Blessed [esher — happy] is the man [ish] that fears [yare] the LORD [YHWH], that delights [chaphets] greatly [meod] in His commandments [mitsvah].
1.notes: halelu-Yah (H1984, H3050), then the acrostic: ashre-ish yare et-YHWH (H835, H376, H3372) — Psalm 111 ended with the fear of the LORD; 112 opens with the man who has it. be-mitsvotav chaphets meod (H4687, H2654, H3966): DELIGHTS, greatly, in the commands — fear and delight in one man, which is the definition of a saint.

2.text: His offspring will be mighty in the land; blessed will be the generation of the upright.
2.amp: His seed [zera] shall be mighty [gibbor] upon earth [eretz]: the generation [dor] of the upright [yashar] shall be blessed [barak].
2.notes: gibbor ba-aretz yihyeh zaro (H1368, H776, H2233): his seed a gibbor, a mighty man, in the land — dor yesharim yevorakh (H1755, H3477, H1288): the generation of the straight ones blessed. Piety as a family inheritance; the covenant runs through households (cf. Psalm 103:17).

3.text: Wealth and riches are in his house, and his righteousness stands forever.
3.amp: Wealth [hon] and riches [osher] shall be in his house [bayith]: and his righteousness [tsedaqah] endures [amad — stands] for ever [ad].
3.notes: hon-va-osher be-beto (H1952, H6239, H1004): substance and riches in the house — the Old Testament does not pretend prosperity is unspiritual — ve-tsidqato omedet la-ad (H6666, H5975, H5703): and the line lifted straight from Psalm 111:3, where it was GOD'S righteousness. The man mirrors his Maker.

4.text: For the upright, light rises up in the darkness — he is gracious, full of compassion, and righteous.
4.amp: Unto the upright [yashar] there arises [zarach — dawns, breaks out] light [or] in the darkness [choshek]: he is gracious [channun], and full of compassion [rachum], and righteous [tsaddiq].
4.notes: zarach ba-choshekh or la-yesharim (H2224, H2822, H216, H3477): light DAWNS in the dark for the upright — zarach is the sunrise verb. channun ve-rachum ve-tsaddiq (H2587, H7349, H6662): Psalm 111:4's description of the LORD, now applied to the man: gracious and compassionate is what a God-fearer turns into.

5.text: It goes well with the man who deals graciously and lends; he manages his affairs with sound judgment.
5.amp: A good [tov] man [ish] shows favour [chanan — deals graciously], and lends [lavah]: he will guide [kul — sustain, manage] his affairs [dabar] with discretion ['judgment', mishpat, the KJV margin].
5.notes: tov-ish chonen u-malveh (H2896, H376, H2603, H3867): the good man is a lender — generous credit to the poor, without the biting interest Psalm 15:5 forbade — yekhalkel debarav be-mishpat (H3557, H1697, H4941): and he sustains his affairs with judgment: generosity is not carelessness.

6.text: Surely he will never be shaken; the righteous will be held in everlasting remembrance.
6.amp: Surely he shall not be moved [mot — toppled] for ever [olam]: the righteous [tsaddiq] shall be in everlasting [olam] remembrance [zeker].
6.notes: ki-le-olam lo-yimmot (H5769, H4131): Psalm 15:5's promise — never toppled — le-zekher olam yihyeh tsaddiq (H2143, H6662): the righteous become a zeker, a memorial, the word Psalm 111:4 used for God's wonders. The good man's life is remembered the way God's works are.

7.text: He will not be afraid of bad news; his heart is fixed, trusting in the LORD.
7.amp: He shall not be afraid [yare] of evil [ra] tidings [shemuah — report, news]: his heart [leb] is fixed [kun — established, steadfast], trusting [batach] in the LORD [YHWH].
7.notes: mi-shemuah raah lo yira (H8052, H7451, H3372): the verse for every phone that rings at night — not that bad news does not come, but that it does not command him. nakhon libbo batuach ba-YHWH (H3559, H3820, H982, H3068): the heart set firm by kun, like Psalm 57:7's, and the firmness has an object: trusting in the LORD, not in the news being good.

8.text: His heart is held steady; he will not be afraid, until he looks upon his adversaries in triumph.
8.amp: His heart [leb] is established [samak — upheld], he shall not be afraid [yare], until he see [raah] his desire upon his enemies [tsar — adversaries].
8.notes: samukh libbo lo yira (H5564, H3820, H3372): the leaning-verb — his heart is propped, as Psalm 111:8 said the precepts are — ad asher-yireh be-tsarav (H7200, H6862): until he looks on his adversaries, the survivor's steady gaze of Psalm 118:7. Fearlessness with a deadline: until the trouble is over.

9.text: He has scattered freely; he has given to the poor; his righteousness stands forever; his horn will be lifted up in honor.
9.amp: He has dispersed [pazar — scattered abroad], he has given [natan] to the poor [evyon]; his righteousness [tsedaqah] endures [amad] for ever [ad]; his horn [qeren] shall be exalted [rum] with honour [kabod].
9.notes: pizzar natan la-evyonim (H6340, H5414, H34): SCATTERED — the sower's verb, seed flung wide — to the needy; Paul quotes this line for the Corinthians' offering (cf. 2 Corinthians 9:9). tsidqato omedet la-ad (H6666, H5975, H5703) for the second time; qarno tarum be-khabod (H7161, H7311, H3519): the horn raised in honor — generosity is how a man's strength gets lifted.

10.text: The wicked will see it and be furious; he will grind his teeth and melt away. The craving of the wicked will come to nothing.
10.amp: The wicked [rasha] shall see [raah] it, and be grieved [kaas — vexed, angry]; he shall gnash [charaq] with his teeth [shen], and melt away [masas]: the desire [taavah — craving] of the wicked [rasha] shall perish [abad].
10.notes: rasha yireh ve-khaas (H7563, H7200, H3707): the other man, watching — shinnav yacharoq ve-namas (H8127, H2786, H4549): teeth ground, then melted like wax. taavat reshaim toved (H8378, H6). The acrostic's last letter falls on the wicked man's craving: what the God-fearer's righteousness does forever (vv. 3, 9), the wicked's desire cannot do at all.
